events.title: Queen Victoria Establishes the Victoria Cross
events.description: Queen Victoria issued a royal warrant creating the Victoria Cross, a medal to recognize acts of exceptional valour by British military personnel.
events.significance: The Victoria Cross became the highest military honour in the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth, and it has stood as a symbol of courage for almost 170 years.

events.title: Kansas Joins the Union
events.description: Kansas was admitted as the 34th state of the United States, entering the Union as a free state on the eve of the Civil War.
events.significance: Kansas's admission followed years of violent conflict over slavery, known as 'Bleeding Kansas'. It tipped the balance further toward free states as the nation approached war.

events.title: Karl Benz Patents the Automobile
events.description: German engineer Karl Benz filed a patent for his gas-powered vehicle, the Benz Patent-Motorwagen, a three-wheeled machine powered by an internal combustion engine.
events.significance: The patent is widely regarded as the birth certificate of the modern automobile. It started an industry that reshaped cities, economies and daily life around the world.

events.title: Birth of Anton Chekhov
events.description: Anton Chekhov, the Russian physician and writer, was born on this day in Taganrog. He became a master of the short story and a leading playwright.
events.significance: His plays, including The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard, and his stories transformed modern drama and short fiction. Writers and theatre-makers still draw on his work.

events.title: Birth of Oprah Winfrey
events.description: Oprah Winfrey, who became a talk show host, producer, actress and media entrepreneur, was born on this day in Mississippi.
events.significance: She built one of the most influential media careers in history. She founded the OWN network and became a leading figure in television and philanthropy.
